traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Scrophulariaceae, which takes in Schlegeliaceae: leaves alternate, opposite or whorled; leaves usually simple, rarely compound; margins entire, crenate, serrate or dentate; veins pinnate or palmate; stipules absent; leaf rosettes basal or none, sometimes terminal; plants hermaphrodite; flowers turned over usually absent, rarely present; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary, in cymes, in racemes, in spikes, in heads or in panicles; flowers zygomorphic; irregular flowers bilabiate; perianth sepals and petals; fruit usually capsule, rarely berry; stamens (2-) 4 (-5); carpels 2 (-3). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
